thesis_health.reason: Four of five core assumptions have credible confirmation evidence, while domestic-demand transmission remains the principal weak link.

scenarios.description: Orderly normalization, durable wage growth, capital-allocation reform, and broader domestic demand improve earnings quality across financials, reform beneficiaries, and selected exporters.
Nominal growth and reform continue, but real-income pressure, currency volatility, geopolitical costs, and valuation dispersion produce mixed company outcomes.
exit_conditions: Broad real-income improvement moves the regime toward bull
Policy or earnings stress moves the regime toward bear

scenarios.description: Policy error, renewed real-income deterioration, global demand weakness, or financial-market stress undermines normalization and earnings breadth.

decision.summary: The first evidence-based review supports an intact JPY thesis and identifies three named companies requiring current valuation discipline.
required_actions: Monitor real wages and household consumption.
Track BOJ normalization and JGB-market stress.
Maintain price-based discipline for MUFG, ITOCHU, and Toyota.

developments.title: BOJ maintained the policy rate at 1.0 percent after the June increase
developments.fact: The BOJ retained a gradual normalization posture while acknowledging inflation risks.
developments.interpretation: Normalization remains orderly, but the risk of policy or currency volatility is rising.
developments.action: Monitor JGB volatility, credit costs, deposit pricing, and the September policy meeting.

developments.title: Nominal wages continued to grow while real-income confirmation remained incomplete
developments.fact: Average cash earnings increased approximately 3.4 percent year over year in June 2026, but household purchasing-power improvement remained uneven.
developments.interpretation: Nominal reflation is established, but domestic-demand breadth still requires real-wage confirmation.
developments.action: Review official real-wage and household-spending releases.

developments.title: Inflation and nominal activity remained above the pre-reflation regime
developments.fact: The all-items CPI index was 113.6 in June 2026 and nominal GDP was approximately 675.6 trillion yen in the January-March period.
developments.interpretation: Japan has not returned to the former deflationary regime.
developments.action: Monitor inflation composition and real household income.

developments.title: Japan finalized the 2026 Corporate Governance Code revision
developments.fact: The revision and updated TSE guidance sharpen expectations for capital allocation and cost-of-capital discipline.
developments.interpretation: Governance reform remains an active structural return engine rather than a completed event.
developments.action: Track repurchases, dividends, cross-shareholding reductions, and ROE targets.

developments.title: Selected companies demonstrated multiple return engines but uneven currency dependence
developments.fact: MUFG benefited from higher yen rates and fee growth, ITOCHU reported broad core-profit growth and buybacks, and Toyota produced strong net income with a material foreign-exchange contribution.
developments.interpretation: Financials and governance beneficiaries have stronger independent engines than exporters whose earnings remain heavily currency-assisted.
developments.action: Use company-specific valuation and currency-normalized scenarios.

scorecard.name: Nominal growth remains positive
scorecard.assessment: Wages, CPI, nominal GDP, and company revenue support the reflation regime.

scorecard.name: BOJ normalization remains orderly
scorecard.assessment: Normalization has progressed without broad credit stress, but policy and currency volatility are rising.

scorecard.name: Governance reform improves capital allocation
scorecard.assessment: Revised governance rules, buybacks, and explicit capital-efficiency expectations provide strong confirmation.

scorecard.name: Domestic demand improves
scorecard.assessment: Nominal wages are positive, but durable real-income and consumption improvement are not fully established.

scorecard.name: Select exporters retain pricing power
scorecard.assessment: Toyota shows product and hybrid strength, but foreign exchange remains a large reported-profit driver.

catalysts.name: Further BOJ normalization
catalysts.confirmation_test: Higher rates without material credit deterioration, destabilizing JGB volatility, or destructive deposit competition.
catalysts.failure_test: Funding stress, rising credit losses, or disorderly yield volatility.

catalysts.name: Real-wage inflection
catalysts.confirmation_test: Several months of positive real wages accompanied by stronger consumption and services demand.
catalysts.failure_test: Nominal wage growth continues to lag household inflation and mandatory costs.

catalysts.name: Governance-code implementation
catalysts.confirmation_test: Measurable balance-sheet deployment, cross-shareholding reductions, repurchases, dividends, and higher ROE targets.
catalysts.failure_test: Disclosure improves without changes in capital allocation or returns.

catalysts.name: Yen stabilization
catalysts.confirmation_test: Reduced volatility with exporters maintaining margins through price, mix, or productivity.
catalysts.failure_test: Abrupt appreciation damages exporter margins or renewed depreciation intensifies household inflation.

opportunities.name: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group
opportunities.catalyst: Further net-interest-income growth and progress toward the 2.7 trillion yen net-income target.
opportunities.main_risk: Normalization expectations and earnings growth are already substantially reflected in the share price.
opportunities.next_action: Maintain valuation review and wait for a larger margin of safety.

company_review.reason: Highest-ranked named company with direct normalization exposure and multiple independent earnings engines.

opportunities.name: ITOCHU Corporation
opportunities.catalyst: Delivery of the 950 billion yen profit forecast and execution of the 300 billion yen repurchase.
opportunities.main_risk: The current multiple discounts sustained high returns, successful investment deployment, and limited portfolio impairment.
opportunities.next_action: Wait for an attractive entry or higher normalized earnings.

company_review.reason: Broad non-resource growth and capital-allocation reform create multiple engines, but valuation requires discipline.

opportunities.name: Toyota Motor Corporation
opportunities.catalyst: Hybrid volume growth, operating-margin stabilization, and execution of the 1 trillion yen repurchase.
opportunities.main_risk: Foreign exchange is a material profit driver and underlying operating income declined in the latest quarter.
opportunities.next_action: Monitor currency-normalized margins before increasing exposure.

company_review.reason: The strongest eligible exporter candidate with product and scale advantages beyond currency translation.

opportunities.name: Japanese financial normalization
opportunities.main_risk: Deposit competition, duration losses, and credit costs.

opportunities.name: Trading houses and capital-allocation reform
opportunities.catalyst: Further asset rotation and shareholder distributions.
opportunities.main_risk: Commodity cycles and overpayment for growth assets.

opportunities.name: Quality exporters with pricing power
opportunities.catalyst: Margin resilience under a more stable or stronger yen.
opportunities.main_risk: Earnings depend primarily on foreign-exchange translation.

ranked_company_reviews.selection_reason: Direct normalization exposure combined with loan, fee, overseas, Morgan Stanley, and capital-return engines.
Broad core-profit growth, non-resource exposure, portfolio optimization, governance reform, and shareholder returns.
Hybrid leadership, brand, scale, pricing, and capital returns provide independent engines beyond foreign exchange.

risks.name: Persistent real-wage weakness
risks.trigger: Nominal wages continue to lag household inflation and mandatory costs.

risks.name: Disorderly BOJ tightening
risks.trigger: JGB volatility, funding costs, credit losses, and leveraged-sector stress rise together.

risks.name: Governance backsliding
risks.trigger: Revised rules result in disclosure without balance-sheet action or higher returns.

risks.name: Currency-dependent exporter earnings
risks.trigger: Exporter earnings deteriorate sharply under a stronger yen without offsetting price, mix, or productivity.

risks.name: Global demand shock
risks.trigger: Broad deterioration in exports, trading-house earnings, credit quality, and earnings revisions.

next_decision_points.decision_test: Assess consumer-electronics demand, pricing, and currency sensitivity.
Determine whether normalization remains gradual and financially stable.
Test core-profit breadth, investment deployment, and shareholder-return execution.
Separate volume, pricing, mix, and productivity from foreign exchange.
Review deposit beta, credit costs, capital returns, and progress toward the full-year target.

research_backlog.question: Do final June and July real-wage and household-spending data confirm improving purchasing power?
Are higher policy rates increasing bank earnings without destabilizing deposits, credit quality, or JGB markets?
How much capital reallocation is attributable to durable governance change rather than cyclical buybacks?
What are Toyota and ITOCHU earnings under normalized currency assumptions?

publication.summary: The first evidence-based JPY review supports an intact thesis with a fair scenario, 78 thesis health, and MUFG, ITOCHU, and Toyota selected for company analysis.
